chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, who said:

I entered upon Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام when his elder son Isma'il had died, and he began kissing him while he was dead. So I said: May I be made your ransom, is it not the case that a dead person should not be touched after he dies, and whoever touches him must perform ghusl (ritual bath)? He said: “As long as his warmth remains, there is no problem; that only applies when he has become cold.”

key_terms.اَلْغُسْلُ: ritual bath required in certain states of impurity
key_terms.بَرَدَ: when the body has become cold
key_terms.بِحَرَارَتِهِ: while the body's warmth is still present

ai.seo_question: Does touching a deceased person require ghusl (ritual bath) immediately after death?
ai.summary: This hadith relates that Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام kissed his deceased son Isma'il after his death. When asked about touching the dead and the obligation of ghusl (ritual bath), the Imam عليه السلام clarified that there is no issue so long as the body's warmth remains, and the ruling applies once the body has become cold.
